job.title: Director of Policy and Advocacy - auDA
job.description:
Director, Policy & Advocacy - auDA


  • Lead policy development and advocacy shaping Australia's internet future in a global context
  • Influence government  regulation and facilitate multi-stakeholder policy outcomes
  • Strategic leadership opportunity with a nationally significant, purpose-driven organisation

 


About auDA


.au Domain Administration Limited (auDA) is the administrator of Australia's .au domain name system (DNS), a critical component of the nation's communications infrastructure relied upon by internet users in Australia and internationally.


As a not-for-profit, community-based organisation endorsed by the Australian Government, auDA plays an important role in ensuring the secure, stable and reliable operation of .au while championing an open, free, secure and interoperable internet for the benefit of all Australians.


auDA's purpose is to connect Australians to an open internet with trust and confidence. Its responsibilities extend beyond domain administration to developing transparent and responsive .au policies, supporting multi-stakeholder internet governance and contributing to national and international policy discussions.

Guided by its 2026–30 Strategy, auDA is strengthening its capability across four strategic pillars — Trust, Innovation, Impact and Capability — to respond to an increasingly complex digital, technological and geopolitical environment.

 


About the Director, Policy & Advocacy Role


Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director, Policy & Advocacy is a senior leadership opportunity responsible for shaping auDA's internet policy development,  advocacy and advisory based in internet governance principles across domestic, regional and international environments.


The appointment comes at an important time as auDA evolves its organisational structure and repositions its policy and advocacy capability. With the Internet Governance function positioned as a core function within Operations, the Director will play a central role in establishing clear policy priorities, strengthening engagement with industry, community and government, and developing a high-performing policy team.


A particular focus will be advancing auDA's influence on Australian legislative and regulatory developments affecting the digital economy. This includes emerging issues relating to cybersecurity, privacy, online safety and digital duty of care, scams prevention, artificial intelligence and the security of critical infrastructure.

The Director will lead multi-stakeholder policy development processes relating to the .au licensing framework and broader internet policy matters, ensuring that auDA's positions are evidence-based, practical and responsive to the needs of Australian internet users.


The role will also represent auDA contributing to global internet governance processes through various forums to develop and influence on auDA’s policy positions.

Working closely with the Chief Operating Officer, Executive Leadership Team and Board, the Director will provide high-quality advice on emerging legislative and policy issues, establish productive relationships across community, government, industry and technical communities, and lead the development of auDA's policy and advocacy capability.



About You


You are an accomplished policy and advocacy leader with demonstrated experience analysing complex legislative and regulatory issues, developing evidence-based policy positions and influencing meaningful policy outcomes.


You bring substantial experience leading policy development processes involving diverse stakeholders, balancing competing perspectives and translating complex technical, regulatory or legislative matters into clear and practical advice for senior decision-makers.


Importantly, you have a demonstrated ability to work with industry and advocate for changes to national legislation and influence government policy development. You understand how to engage effectively with policymakers, regulators, industry representatives and other stakeholders to build consensus and achieve outcomes.


You are a confident and credible communicator, capable of preparing high-quality policy submissions, strategic briefings and recommendations for executives, Boards and government stakeholders. Your approach combines intellectual rigour, sound judgement and an appreciation of the practical implications of policy decisions.


As a leader, you are collaborative, curious and outcomes-focused, with experience building capability, developing teams and fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. You are comfortable navigating complex stakeholder environments and engaging constructively with differing perspectives.

Experience in  internet technology, digital regulation or critical infrastructure would be highly regarded, however, specialist internet governance expertise is not essential. Candidates with strong transferable policy development and legislative advocacy experience, together with the ability to work effectively with technical subject matter experts, are encouraged to apply.


Experience influencing international policy would also be advantageous.


Relevant tertiary qualifications in public policy, law, political science, international relations, technology or a related discipline are desirable.

job.title: Program Director – Centre of Excellence in Disability Inclusion (CoEDI) - The Gordon
job.description:
Program Director – Centre of Excellence in Disability Inclusion (CoEDI) - The Gordon


  • Establish and lead a nationally significant Centre of Excellence in Disability Inclusion
  • Shape national practice and drive system-wide change across vocational education and training
  • Turn innovation and lived experience into better education and employment opportunities



About The Gordon


The Gordon is a dynamic and inclusive organisation and a thriving community where people connect and work together to inspire students. With a strong commitment to creating the future, The Gordon provides a rich and rewarding environment where every student has the opportunity to succeed.


At The Gordon, everyone is welcomed, valued and empowered to make a difference. Its culture is underpinned by the values We are The Gordon, We bring our best, We create the future and We are student minded, which guide how its people work, make decisions and support its students.


Centre of Excellence in Disability Inclusion


Supported by a $36 million Victorian Government investment, The Gordon’s Centre of Excellence in Disability Inclusion (CoEDI) is a major initiative to improve access, participation and success in vocational education and employment for people with disability. With a purpose-built facility at The Gordon’s Geelong City Campus expected to open in 2027, the Centre brings together students, TAFEs, government, industry and community partners to address systemic barriers and strengthen inclusive practice. People with lived experience of disability are central to its design and delivery, ensuring their expertise shapes its priorities and approaches.


The Centre will develop, test and share practical approaches to inclusive teaching and assessment, accessible learning environments and technology, workforce capability and transitions into employment. Combining applied research, innovation and knowledge sharing, it will help embed lasting improvements across The Gordon and the broader TAFE network. This work is already progressing through the Geelong Inclusive Employment Compact, bringing together the TAC, WorkSafe Victoria, the NDIA and Barwon Health to strengthen pathways from training into meaningful work.


About the Program Director Role


This is a rare opportunity to establish and lead a nationally significant Centre of Excellence and help shape the future of disability inclusion across vocational education and training. As Program Director, you will set the Centre’s direction from the outset, build its team and partnerships, and position it as a trusted national leader in inclusive education and employment practice.


Working alongside people with lived experience, you will translate innovation into practical approaches that TAFEs and employers can adopt. You will connect government, education, industry, research and disability sector partners around shared priorities, influence national practice and drive system-wide change that expands opportunities for people with disability.


Reporting to the Executive Director – Growth and Student Experience, you will lead the Centre’s strategy and delivery, with accountability for funded programs, governance, budgets, risk and evaluation.


About You


You are an accomplished senior leader who sees the potential to change how vocational education and employment work for people with disability. You bring the vision to establish a Centre with national influence and the practical leadership to turn that ambition into lasting outcomes.


You have led complex programs, Centres, reform initiatives or portfolios, combining strategic planning, sound governance and delivery. You build trusted relationships across organisational boundaries, navigate complex government environments and bring partners together to influence organisational, system or sector-wide change.


Your commitment to inclusion is evident in how you lead and engage people with lived experience through co-design and consultation. You have built effective multidisciplinary teams, managed budgets, risks and competing priorities, and provided clear advice and reporting to executives, boards and funding bodies.

 

Knowledge of disability inclusion policy and practice, and experience in vocational education and training, tertiary education or another complex public-purpose environment, will be highly regarded. Experience establishing a new function, program or operating model, and working with government funding arrangements, would also be valuable.


A relevant postgraduate qualification and/or equivalent executive leadership experience is required.

job.title: Executive Director – Transformation Program Implementation
job.description:
Executive Director – Transformation Program Implementation

 

  • Lead a significant enterprise-wide transformation agenda, moving from strategy into execution and delivery
  • Shape the future of technology, digital, AI and business reform within a complex, purpose-driven organisation
  • Attractive salary package circa $400,000

 


About our client


Our client delivers important services and outcomes for a diverse community, operating within a complex environment where client outcomes, organisational performance and long-term sustainability are central to its purpose. The organisation is entering an important phase in the delivery of an ambitious transformation agenda. Following significant strategic design, planning and conceptualisation, the focus is now firmly on execution and delivery, supported by technology, digital capability, transformed business processes and a high-performing organisational culture.


The division in which this role leads brings together the organisation’s technology, digital and business reform agenda. Importantly, Technology Operations is an established and operational function within the division. This appointment is therefore focused on leading and optimising existing technology capability while driving the broader enterprise transformation agenda.

 


About the role


Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and operating as a key member of the Executive Leadership Team, the role will lead the organisation’s technology, digital and transformation agenda.


With much of the strategic design, planning and conceptualisation already well developed, the focus is firmly on execution, translating an ambitious transformation agenda into tangible outcomes across systems, processes and culture.


The role will lead major transformation programs, business process redesign and the continued evolution of digital, AI, cyber, data and technology capabilities. You will also provide vision, leadership and governance across IT strategy, technology plans and architecture, ensuring these capabilities remain aligned with organisational priorities and industry best practice.


Working collaboratively with the CEO and executive colleagues, the successful candidate will contribute to whole-of-organisation leadership and help create alignment around shared transformation priorities and outcomes.


 

About You


You are an accomplished executive leader with extensive experience across technology, digital and enterprise transformation, with a demonstrated track record of delivering complex, cross-functional organisational initiatives and transformation programs. You bring highly developed strategic, analytical and commercial capability, with the judgement and delivery focus required to translate strategy into implementation and maintain momentum through complex delivery.


You will bring many years of significant experience leading an information technology and transformation function, including digital capability, strategic planning, technology operations, applications, platforms and infrastructure. You will be comfortable providing executive leadership across technology while maintaining a broader enterprise perspective. Importantly, this opportunity requires more than technical expertise. You will be a collaborative and constructive enterprise leader, able to build trusted relationships at CEO, Board and executive level, navigate complexity, lead specialist teams and create alignment across diverse stakeholders.


You will bring energy, ambition and a genuine appetite for delivery, together with the resilience and adaptability required to lead a significant transformation agenda.
